when: A change touches worker heartbeat, health checking, or re-registration recovery between a worker and the LMCache multiprocess server.
expect: Recovery must not depend on observing an unhealthy-to-healthy transition. The heartbeat must detect a new server incarnation (e.g. a boot token compared against a baseline), or treat a missing-registration response as a trigger to re-register. Seed the baseline synchronously at registration or adapter init, not on the first heartbeat. The first STORE/RETRIEVE must wait for the initial heartbeat check. Require a deterministic test that swaps the server between two successful probes with no unhealthy interval in between. Shutdown must drain in-flight async device operations before unregistering or freeing KV caches.
why: PING only proves the server is reachable. touch_instance ignores unknown instance IDs, and the heartbeat starts lazily. A fast restart can therefore leave the worker unregistered for good, and every later STORE/RETRIEVE fails.
examples: The server restarts between two successful PINGs, re-registration never runs, and STORE fails forever.
The boot token is captured on the first heartbeat after a restart, so the restarted server becomes the baseline.
concern: Detect server restart/incarnation (boot token) reliably so worker re-registration recovery always triggers
